headline: Three weeks on: 17,048 homes evaluated, 55,212 people affected and 4,428 still in 135 shelters. The government will build 2,700 homes by March 2027. A rain alert to 3 Nov raises landslide risk on 9,500+ quake-loosened slopes.
key_points: Official (SINAPROC, to 28 Oct): 2 deaths, 27 injured; 17,048 homes evaluated; 55,212 people affected; 4,428 people in 135 shelters (down from 5,779 in 154).
Homes with total damage: 3,390 (COE, 24 Oct; not yet updated). Damage concentrated in Los Santos and Herrera, then Veraguas, Coclé and eastern Chiriquí.
Housing: 2,700 new homes planned (1,300 started, 1,400 added on 27 Oct), last keys March 2027; first 300 under way in Herrera; temporary structures next to each site.
Isla Cañas: coast sank 15–30 cm; seawater and sand now flood homes during high tides; government surveying homes and offering relocation to the mainland.
Schools: 619 damaged, 35 destroyed, 85 must be rebuilt entirely, target 3 March 2027; teachers warn of learning gaps.
Infrastructure: 120 health facilities, 127 government buildings, 44 churches and 22 bridges damaged; 3 CSS clinics still closed (Remón, Los Pozos, Tonosí).
Landslides and aftershocks: 9,553 landslides mapped; 1,154 aftershocks; an M5.1 near Tonosí on 29 Oct prompted evacuations in Coclé, no new damage.
Finance: Moody's cites MEF needs of up to ~US$100M (~0.1% of GDP), no rating impact expected; Germany delivered 60 t of aid; 75 businesses report losses.

areas.area: Los Santos (Macaracas, Tonosí, Las Tablas, Pedasí)
areas.text: Most homes evaluated of any province. Isla Cañas and Cañas flooded again by high tides after 15–30 cm subsidence; relocation being offered. Búcaro shows ~1 m surface fault rupture; Tonosí hospital in a modular unit. M5.1 aftershock 24 km NW of Tonosí on 29 Oct.

areas.area: Herrera (Los Pozos, Las Minas, Pesé, Ocú)
areas.text: Large share of destroyed homes and 20 of the 35 collapsed schools (13 in Las Minas, 6 in Los Pozos). First 300 government homes under way; CSS clinic in Los Pozos still closed, care in a modular unit.

Hosts most people in shelters (3,500+). Mariato: 17 schools lost, ~5 km of highway and several bridges damaged, weight limits on five Atalaya–Mariato bridges; Cañazas: 400+ homes affected; Montijo: 33+ homes uninhabitable; Santiago: second death (a school secretary injured during evacuation).

Penonomé cathedral tower and governorship building damaged (the latter may be demolished); Hotel Dos Continentes partly collapsed; homes lost in La Pintada (Agua Fría) and El Bajito de San Miguel. Students will finish the year with guides and modules.
Eastern Chiriquí (San Félix, Remedios, Tolé) and adjoining Ngäbe-Buglé communities: mostly adobe homes damaged; 139 schools affected; reconstruction started in San Félix.

Five floors of Hospital Santo Tomás's old maternity building evacuated; Policlínica Presidente Remón closed; other services back to normal (Metro, Tocumen, ports). Colón: Hospital San Juan and municipal market partly damaged.

services.text: 17,048 homes evaluated, 3,390 destroyed (24 Oct); 4,428 people in 135 shelters. 2,700 new homes planned by March 2027; first 300 under way in Herrera.
Classes back in most regions; 619 schools damaged, 35 destroyed; 85 to be rebuilt by 3 March 2027; UNICEF temporary learning spaces.
120 facilities damaged; CSS: 86% operating normally, Policlínica Remón, CAPPS Los Pozos and ULAPS Tonosí closed (modular care); US$61M for repairs.
22 bridges damaged and 66 road-damage reports being verified; weight limits on five Atalaya–Mariato bridges; MOP repair costs pending. Rain alert to 3 Nov.
Power restored; water restored on Isla Cañas; shortages persist in parts of Azuero.
Tocumen and Metro Lines 1 and 2 operating since 12 Oct; state ports back to ~80%.

upcoming: Coming up: rain alert to 3 Nov (landslides, access); updated count of destroyed homes; MOP road and bridge costs; Moody's rating review in November.
unknowns: Updated count of destroyed homes: SINAPROC's 17,048 evaluations have not been split by damage level since 24 Oct.
Full cost of damage: MEF cites up to ~US$100M of spending needs; MOP road and bridge costs and private losses are not yet included.
Whether Isla Cañas residents will relocate, and where.
Whether heavy rain to 3 Nov triggers new landslides on the 9,500+ mapped slopes.
How many of the 2,700 homes will be ready before the end of 2026.
